title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Preregistered, Artifact-Backed Evaluation of Input-Sanitization and Deterministic Verification Against Adversarial Intents
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured whether template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (and at-most-one automated repair) changes the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations under adversarially mutated intents. The frozen run used the declared generator gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 within the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; complete paired outcomes used in the primary analysis = 141. Observed per-pair acceptance: Baseline 135/141 (95.7447%); Guarded 141/141 (100.0%); paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. We reconcile preregistration language vs the formal estimand, document per-condition pipeline semantics with explicit archived-artifact references, disclose a protocol deviation (unset runtime temperature), and discuss operational interpretation and limitations constrained by synthetic scope and single-model/validator evaluation. All principal numeric claims are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts referenced in Methods and Results.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) can translate operator intent into device CLI, offering potential NetOps productivity gains. However, LLM outputs carry operational risks: syntax/semantic errors, incorrect ordering that violates workflow constraints, and exposure to adversarially crafted inputs that may cause unsafe configurations. Prior prototype work shows that coupling generation with deterministic verification and repair reduces errors in constrained settings, but common evaluation metrics (token-match, BLEU) do not directly measure deployability or safety for device configuration [3,8,9].

This study tests a narrowly scoped operational question with preregistered inferential machinery: How effective are template-based input sanitization and deterministic verifier-gating (with at-most-one automated repair) at changing the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations when inputs are adversarially mutated? We preregistered study cand-2026-03, froze the design, and executed the run under the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter. The experiment intentionally uses shared_initial_candidate semantics so paired comparisons isolate post-generation interventions (sanitization, gating, and repair) rather than changes to the initial generation.
sections.related_work:
Deterministic network-verification tools (Header Space Analysis, NetPlumber, VeriFlow) provide scalable checks of forwarding and configuration invariants and have been used as validators for generated configurations [5–7]. Empirical NetOps studies report that LLMs produce useful drafts but often make ordering, scope, or syntax mistakes; coupling with verifier feedback and localized repair yields prototype improvements [3,8]. Surveys of AIOps and telecommunications identify fragmented evaluation practices and recommend operationally meaningful benchmarks measuring deployability and safety, not just surface text similarity [4,9].

Security analyses document prompt-injection and indirect-prompt attacks that compromise LLM-integrated applications and motivate input-sanitization and gating defenses; tool-augmented orchestration architectures (Toolformer-style) demonstrate practical patterns for LLMs to call external checks and repair outputs [10,11]. Our experiment situates itself at the intersection of these threads by preregistering a formal paired estimand grounded in verifier acceptance and by publishing per-episode validator traces that enable traceable interpretation against prior prototype claims.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered study cand-2026-03 (preregistration_sha256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373). The primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline: for each adversarial intent the binary outcome equals 1 if deterministic_netops_validator_v5 would accept the final candidate for deployment and 0 otherwise. The confirmatory test is an exact two-sided McNemar; bootstrap percentile 95% CIs use 10,000 resamples with seed = 1729 (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl).

Design, task bank and adversary model. The preregistration specified N = 150 adversarial intents (paired episodes across two conditions → planned episodes = 300). The synthetic intent templates exercise admin, MTU, and VLAN changes, safe ordering patterns, and constrained required sequences. Adversarial mutations were deterministic template perturbations (string-level reorderings, token-insertions, and slot overrides) produced by the deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; generator_id, seeds, and task payloads appear in execution/task_manifest.jsonl and representative task artifacts (e.g., execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt). Scope is explicitly limited to these synthetic templates and the deterministic CLI grammar encoded in the validator.

Model, validator, orchestration and declared configuration. The archived run declares declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" (execution/model_configuration.json) and uses deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as the verifier. The orchestration adapter family is hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The run implemented a generate–validate–repair workflow with a template-based input-sanitizer applied to the guarded branch prior to gating. The archived model_configuration.json records max_output_tokens = 1024 and temperature = null; we disclose the unset temperature as a protocol deviation (see Disclosure). Provider-call accounting and stage counts (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) were used to validate that shared_initial_candidate semantics and repair limits were followed.

Pipeline timeline and shared_initial_candidate semantics (artifact-grounded). To address reviewer requests we provide an explicit per-condition timeline with artifact references:
1) Task instantiation and adversarial mutation: execution/task_manifest.jsonl contains per-pair payloads and mutation metadata (e.g., pair_id task-000001). Sanitizer outputs and any slot normalization are recorded in the task_manifest payload when sanitization modifies required slots.
2) Shared initial generation: a single LLM call produced a shared_initial_candidate persisted at execution/responses/task-<id>-shared-initial.txt and referenced by both scoring artifacts for the pair. Evidence: stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 150 and per-episode shared_initial_candidate files referenced in execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json.
3) Baseline scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 evaluated the shared_initial_candidate and produced validation_before/final snapshots archived in execution/scoring/<...>-baseline.json.
4) Guarded branch: the pipeline applied template-based sanitization, invoked the verifier-gate, and—if gating policy allowed—permitted at-most-one automated repair LLM call; repair traces exist where invoked and repair stage_count = 6 (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json).
5) Final validation: the validator re-evaluated repaired candidates (or the sanitized original when no repair was invoked) and recorded the guarded final decision and detailed validator traces archived in execution/scoring/<...>-guarded.json.

Missingness, exclusions and failure handling. The preregistered missingness_plan excludes a paired unit only when both paired runs are technical failures. The archive records completed_episodes = 282, failed_episodes = 18, and complete_pairs_included = 141 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). Provider-call accounting (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) documents hosted_model_call_event_count = 156, completed = 147, failed = 9, and stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 150, repair = 6. These artifact-grounded counts validate adherence to the preregistered calling and retry policy.
sections.results:
Execution aggregates and contingency. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; failed episodes = 18 (execution/execution_manifest.json). The primary confirmatory analysis used 141 complete pairs (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). Condition summary (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline_successes = 135/141 (0.9574468085106383); guarded_successes = 141/141 (1.0). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is: n11 = 135, n10 = 6 (guarded=1, baseline=0), n01 = 0, n00 = 0.

Inferential outcomes. Exact two-sided McNemar on the observed paired outcomes yields p = 0.03125. Point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165. The 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) is [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]; these parameters and outputs are archived in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl and analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg and the paired table used for bootstrapping is analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv.

Discordant-case diagnostics and repair accounting. The six discordant n10 pairs are traceable to repair-stage activity. analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json records repair = 6 and stage_counts.repair = 6. Per-episode scoring artifacts (execution/scoring/task-00000X-*.json) contain validation_before and validation_after objects showing that sanitization and/or the permitted repair altered command ordering or normalization such that the final candidate passed deterministic_netops_validator_v5 whereas the unguarded shared_initial_candidate failed. Representative artifacts: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt, execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json, execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json show identical shared_initial_candidate references and the validator snapshots that explain the discordant outcome.

Missingness sensitivity. Nine pairs were both-run technical failures and excluded per preregistered plan (missingness_summary.csv: both_missing_pairs = 9). Under a conservative sensitivity mapping both-missing pairs to failures, baseline acceptance becomes 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded acceptance becomes 141/150 = 0.9400; these recalculated ratios are simple aggregations of archived counts and are reported to illustrate the impact of excluded pairs. The primary inference preserves the preregistered exclusion rule and uses the 141 complete pairs.
sections.discussion:
Reconciliation of preregistration wording and formal estimand. The preregistration's natural-language H1 stated that verifier-gating would reduce attacker-success (fewer unsafe configurations accepted). The formal estimand registered and analyzed measures paired validator acceptance-for-deployment (guarded − baseline). These are distinct constructs: an increase in validator acceptance can reflect successful repair of malformed drafts (reducing operator labor) rather than enabling attacker success. Our observed data show an absolute increase in acceptance (≈4.255 percentage points) because sanitizer/repair recovered reparable drafts that the baseline validator rejected. Therefore, the preregistered natural-language attacker-success claim is not supported by the formal-estimand outcome; we report and interpret the formal estimand explicitly and caution against conflating validator acceptance with attacker-centric safety without an independent semantic-safety oracle.

Operational implications and repair–gate co-design. In this synthetic setting, input sanitization plus limited automated repair can recover valid, deployable configurations that unguarded generation fails to produce. Deterministic gating provides a safety boundary, but its operational effect depends on repair scope and validator coverage. The six discordant cases illustrate a trade-off: repairs enabled acceptance but could—under different validator encodings—accept outputs that are semantically unsafe. Therefore, operational deployment requires co-design of gating rules, constrained repair policies, and richer validator specifications (for example, protocol-level reachability checks) beyond the CLI-syntax and ordering invariants encoded in deterministic_netops_validator_v5.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: 18 technical failures reduced effective sample size and triggered the preregistered exclusion rule (both-run failures = 9). Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 encodes CLI grammar, required sequences, and protected-interface invariants but omits some protocol-level dynamic semantics; acceptance-for-deployment is therefore a partial proxy for operational safety. External validity: single-generator (gpt-5-mini), single-validator, and synthetic intents limit generalization across vendors, protocols, and production traffic. Conclusion validity: the observed absolute effect is small against a high baseline (ceiling effect); detectability does not imply broad practical impact. All of these limitations are supported by the archived artifacts and counts referenced above.

Reproducibility and protocol deviation. The execution/model_configuration.json recorded temperature = null (unset). We treat this as a protocol deviation because provider defaults may affect sampling behavior. To preserve paired comparability despite the unset parameter, the pipeline used shared_initial_candidate semantics (single shared generation per pair) so both baseline and guarded scoring began from the identical initial candidate; stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 150 and provider-call accounting (hosted_model_call_event_count = 156, completed = 147, failed = 9) corroborate the actual call pattern (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json). For deterministic reproduction we recommend explicitly setting temperature = 0 and re-running execution/task_manifest.jsonl under identical provider semantics. The run archive (execution/execution_manifest.json, execution/model_configuration.json, analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) contains the necessary artifact references to repeat the paired-call pattern under an explicit temperature setting.

Recommended next steps grounded in artifacts. (1) Execute the preregistered benign-control (M = 50) to measure false-positive blocking: the preregistration specified this secondary estimand but the archive shows it was not executed (absence visible in execution manifest). (2) Preregister and evaluate an attacker-centric estimand that couples validator acceptance with an independent semantic-safety oracle or operational reachability checks (the current artifacts show that validator acceptance alone cannot establish attacker success). (3) Diversify generators and validators across vendors and CLI dialects and set explicit sampling parameters (temperature = 0) for deterministic reproducibility. (4) Expand validator coverage to protocol-level semantics where feasible. Each recommendation follows directly from artifact-grounded gaps visible in the archived manifests and counts.
sections.conclusion: A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment on a synthetic adversarial intent bank found that template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating and at-most-one automated repair produced a small but statistically detectable absolute increase in deterministic-validator-accepted LLM-generated configurations under the archived formal estimand (paired difference ≈ 0.04255; p = 0.03125; 95% CI [0.01418, 0.07801]). Provider-call accounting and per-episode validator traces indicate the six discordant pairs were associated with permitted repair calls that enabled acceptance. This formal-estimand improvement does not equate to measured reduction in attacker-success under attacker-centric definitions. The run is limited by synthetic scope, a single model/validator, and a protocol deviation (unset runtime temperature). Future work should execute the preregistered benign-control, measure attacker-centric estimands with an independent semantic-safety oracle, diversify models/validators, and set explicit sampling parameters for reproducible deterministic runs. All principal numbers and reconciliation claims above are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts referenced in Methods and Results (noted artifact paths appear in the Disclosure Statement).

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock under the archived master prompt (provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; all literature review, preregistration, study selection, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer-review cycles, manuscript drafting, and revision reported here were performed autonomously after the lock. Declared models/tools and orchestration: primary generator = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json), deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5, orchestration adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration: study cand-2026-03 was preregistered and archived prior to observing outcomes (preregistration_sha256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373). Protocol deviation: the archived run recorded an unset runtime sampling temperature (temperature = null in execution/model_configuration.json); this is disclosed as a deviation because provider-side defaults may affect sampling determinism. To preserve paired comparability the pipeline used shared_initial_candidate semantics (single shared generation per pair) and provider-call accounting documented in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json confirms the actual call pattern (shared_initial_generation = 150; repair = 6). Key archived artifact references (examples): execution/task_manifest.jsonl; execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt; execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json; execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json; analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; analysis/condition_summary.csv; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl; execution/model_configuration.json; execution/execution_manifest.json. No human manually edited or corrected the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated.
A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; results are reported and interpreted with respect to the archived formal estimand.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
